title: Historical Catalog Entry Analytics

variables.name: type
variables.reason: Movie and TV catalog-entry lags differ; estimate those metadata associations explicitly.
variables.treatment: Encode Movie/TV Show; retain separate duration units.

variables.name: country
variables.reason: Production origins can be associated with historical catalog-entry patterns.
variables.treatment: Tokenize multiple countries; fit vocabulary on the fitting data only.

variables.name: listed_in
variables.reason: Genres may explain variation in observed catalog-entry lags without using target ingredients.
variables.treatment: Tokenize multiple genres; unknown categories do not extend the fitted vocabulary.

variables.name: duration
variables.reason: Film length and season count provide format context independent of release/addition dates.
variables.treatment: Parse positive minutes for Movies and integer seasons for TV Shows; never treat them as interchangeable.

variables.name: release_year
variables.reason: Part of the target formula; using it as a predictor would reveal the target.
variables.treatment: Excluded from prediction; used only to calculate the calendar-year difference.

variables.name: date_added
variables.reason: Measures catalog entry, not original release.
variables.treatment: Build target and chronological partitions; excluded from model inputs.

variables.name: rating
variables.reason: Advisory ratings are not viewer scores, commercial success or clustering ground truth.
variables.treatment: Never used as a model feature or performance label.

variables.name: director
variables.reason: Director credits and missingness describe content metadata associations.
variables.treatment: Director count and missingness indicators only; names do not create a credit vocabulary.

variables.name: show_id / title
variables.reason: Trace records and remove repeated entities; unique identifiers do not describe generalizable content.
variables.treatment: Exclude from features; title/type/year supports entity review.

variables.name: lag_years
variables.reason: Observed calendar-year difference between catalog addition and release, because actual commercial success is unavailable.
variables.treatment: year(date_added) - release_year; remove 14 negative values; retain the long tail.

decisions.reason: The dataset has no views, engagement, revenue or viewer score; commercial success cannot be measured.
decisions.evidence: The target is year(date_added) minus release_year, with explicit input exclusions.
decisions.limitation: Calendar-year difference is not exact elapsed time, prospective waiting time or success.

decisions.reason: release_year and date_added construct the label; including them would leak its value.
decisions.evidence: Feature allowlist excludes release/addition years, dates, identifiers and target.
decisions.limitation: Snapshot survivorship and metadata associations prevent causal or current-acquisition claims.

stages.name: Source validation
stages.reason: Verify the supplied SHA-256, schema, types and duration units.

stages.name: Entity deduplication
stages.reason: Remove 7 repeated entities with a recorded mapping.

stages.name: Target eligibility
stages.reason: Audit and exclude 14 negative calendar-year differences; do not invent corrections or trim the positive tail.

partitions.name: Training through 2019
partitions.purpose: Chronological training; rolling-year validation fits only earlier observations.

partitions.name: Test: 2020–2021
partitions.purpose: Untouched later-year test; the serving model remains trained on training rows only.

partitions.name: Eligible catalog segment: movies
partitions.purpose: Descriptive target statistics across the eligible catalog, not held-out prediction errors.

partitions.name: Eligible catalog segment: tv
partitions.purpose: Descriptive target statistics across the eligible catalog, not held-out prediction errors.

partitions.name: Held-out test segment: Movie
partitions.purpose: Computed from frozen test_predictions.csv; errors measured in calendar years.

partitions.name: Held-out test segment: TV Show
partitions.purpose: Computed from frozen test_predictions.csv; errors measured in calendar years.

split_strategy: Chronological regression: 5,395 training through 2019 / 3,374 test in 2020–2021, from 8,769 eligible entities. Group-wise errors remain visible.
limitations: This is the supplied historical catalog snapshot, not a current Netflix data feed.
Decisions are concise, evidence-backed summaries; model outputs do not establish causation.
